sources.citation: Harvey, Mark (1992). The Gaagudju people and their language. PhD thesis, University of Queensland. Section 1.4 'Languages spoken in the area', pp. 12-13.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Coins 'Giimbiyu' as cover term; 'I have examined recordings in Erre, Mengerrdji and Urningangk and recorded some vocabulary from speakers with a very limited partial knowledge'; confirms three dialects of one language. No phonology or stress of Giimbiyu.

sources.citation: Campbell, Lauren (2006). A Sketch Grammar of Urningangk, Erre and Mengerrdji: the Giimbiyu languages of Western Arnhem Land. Honours thesis, University of Melbourne, vi+115 pp.
sources.tag: likely states stress; not yet obtained
sources.access_detail: open link recorded by Glottolog or the catalog, not checked; access check: not located online or in the libraries checked; the linked copy was not accessible when a reader tried
sources.note: Only grammar sketch of the language (Glottolog's sole descriptive ref for erre1238/mang1382/urni1239); a 115-page sketch with a phonology chapter is the most likely place for a stress statement. Held at MPI-EVA library (PL 7101 CAM 2006) and in the closed Hammarström PDF collection; not deposited in Minerva Access.

sources.citation: Birch, Bruce (2006). A first dictionary of Erre, Mengerrdji and Urningangk: three languages from the Alligator Rivers Region of North Western Arnhem Land, Northern Territory. Jabiru: Gundjeihmi Aboriginal Corporation.
sources.tag: likely states stress; not yet obtained
sources.access_detail: print only (no digital copy found when the work was looked up)
sources.note: Community dictionary by a field linguist who recorded the last speakers; dictionaries of this type usually carry a 'sounds and spelling' introduction that states stress placement; it is the cited source of the Wikipedia phoneme tables. Likely held by AIATSIS and Library & Archives NT.

sources.citation: AIATSIS audio/manuscript holdings for Erre, Mengerrdji and Urningangk (recordings examined by Harvey 1992; possible Kinslow Harris 1960s field notes on Mangerr named by our earlier survey for mang1382).
sources.tag: likely states stress; not yet obtained
sources.note: Harvey 1992 reports existing recordings in all three dialects; the earlier scan note for Mangerr cites Kinslow Harris phonology notes; AUSTLANG (N55 Erre, N220 Giimbiyu) would list them but is could not be reached by automated download.
